thread:
Ravi: Heads-up  SparkWorks reported lower energy-normalized throughput on their new S-series proto when running our rp-lite with kernel k-optim and q4x. Can we triage? @Sofia

Sofia (SparkWorks): Run id SW-2026-05-12-proto. Measured 86 tok/s @ 310W -> 0.277 tok/W. Baseline we gave them was ~0.33 tok/W (seq=512, batch=1). Cmd: `./spark-bench --model rp-lite --seq 512 --batch 1 --quant q4x --kernel k-optim --warmup 30`. NVML=1s.

Devon: Quick checklist: 1) Was DVFS forced? 2) Any priming/short-context mixes? 3) NVML sampling consistent?

Sofia (SparkWorks): NVML 1s, DVFS stock (auto), no priming. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-partners/sparkworks/SW-2026-05-12/.

Nina: If DVFS auto, card might have chosen eco profile. Can you re-run with explicit powercap 360W and warmup 200 (no priming)? Also capture hw counters: memcpy_stall,l2_miss. Use: `./rdw-collector --counters memcpy_stall,l2_miss --out perf.json`

bench-bot: job SW-2026-05-13-repro queued. Artifacts will land at s3://redwood-partners/sparkworks/SW-2026-05-13/ when done.

Sofia (SparkWorks): Re-run done. Early numbers: k-optim+q4x -> 110 tok/s @ 335W -> 0.328 tok/W. k-legacy+q4x -> 112 tok/s @ 332W -> 0.337 tok/W. Perf counters show memcpy spikes at token boundaries for k-optim.

Devon: That pattern suggests kernel introduced extra host<->device copies at step boundaries. Can you attach kernel compile flags and runtime mode (unified mem on/off)?

Sofia (SparkWorks): Flags: "-O3 -DK_OPTIM -march=native". Unified mem disabled. Logs and perf.json uploaded.

Nina: Good. Action plan: 1) SparkWorks to try k-optim with EVICT_DISABLE=1 and re-run. 2) We'll add checklist item to partner-runbook: "energy-normalized throughput validation: seq=512,batch=1,warmup>=200,nvml=1s,powercap explicit,perf-counters,kernel+quant A/B". 3) Hold marketplace card until validated artifact.

Ravi: I'll draft the embargo slide once we get the EVICT_DISABLE results. Thanks everyone.
